reflections.summary: The 2-0 series win is authoritative; the supplied evidence shows Game 2 was won by a well-suited four and clean execution, with no recorded decision errors. The central game-winning sequence was removing Focus Sash Mamoswine, then using Milotic’s Icy Wind speed control, Scrafty’s Close Combat pressure, and Mega Alakazam’s Psychic KOs on Altaria and Choice Scarf Sneasler to leave Milotic in a favorable endgame against weakened Archaludon. Milotic repeatedly survived Thunderbolt through Sitrus Berry and Recover, then Scald burned and eventually finished the Leftovers Archaludon. Talonflame’s Tailwind and Taunt created early tempo and denied Altaria’s support, even though Talonflame was traded for Archaludon pressure. The Game 2 bring of Mega Alakazam, Talonflame, Milotic, and Scrafty fit the revealed opposing four well; Mega Alakazam was the appropriate Mega choice because it provided the immediate speed and Psychic pressure needed to remove Altaria and Sneasler. The evidence does not provide Game 1 details or explicitly identify between-game changes, so their effect cannot be separately credited or blamed. The registered six appear broadly reasonable from this game, but there is insufficient set information or battle evidence to establish that an unbrought roster member offered a materially better four-Pokemon configuration.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series, retain the basic Mega Alakazam/Talonflame/Milotic/Scrafty structure if the same opposing core appears, but make preserving Milotic for Archaludon the highest priority. Continue to Taunt Altaria early when possible, respect Helping Hand-boosted Ice Shard into Mega Alakazam, and use Icy Wind plus Fighting pressure to force Archaludon into a Recover/Protect cycle before committing Alakazam. Avoid relying on Talonflame to remain on the field once Archaludon is in position to Thunderbolt it; its early Tailwind and Taunt value is often enough. No evidence supports replacing the selected Mega or definitively changing the four from this game.
reflections.notebook: Opponent revealed Altaria as Timid Cloud Nine with Tailwind, Helping Hand, Moonblast, and Protect; it supported Mamoswine and Archaludon with Helping Hand and is vulnerable to Taunt and Icy Wind. Mamoswine is Adamant Thick Fat with Focus Sash, Icicle Crash, High Horsepower, Ice Shard, and Protect; account for Helping Hand Ice Shard against frail targets. Archaludon is Modest Stamina with Leftovers, Flash Cannon, Dragon Pulse, Thunderbolt, and Protect. Thunderbolt is its main Milotic pressure; Stamina makes repeated physical contact progressively worse, but Milotic can Recover through Thunderbolts and Scald can create a decisive burn endgame. Sneasler is Jolly Choice Scarf with Unburden, Close Combat, Poison Jab, Coaching, and Upper Hand; Mega Alakazam threatens an immediate Psychic KO. The unrevealed-in-game back line was Life Orb Flash Fire Armarouge with Armor Cannon/Aura Sphere/Energy Ball/Protect and Mental Herb Armor Tail Farigiraf with Imprison/Trick Room/Helping Hand/Psychic Noise. Prep conclusion: speed control, Altaria disruption, and a protected Milotic endgame are strong priorities into this opponent.

reflections.summary: You lost because the early pressure on Mega Alakazam and Talonflame did not become a decisive advantage: Milotic repeatedly used Icy Wind and Recover, while Taunt limited Altaria and Scald eventually burned Archaludon. Sneasler was exposed to Mega Alakazam's Psychic instead of being preserved for a safer cleanup, and Archaludon could not finish the Milotic endgame. The four brought were reasonable but imperfect: Mamoswine and Altaria supplied useful Alakazam pressure and support, while Archaludon strongly threatened Milotic; however, the composition was vulnerable to Taunt, repeated speed control, and Psychic pressure. No Mega Stone holder was evolved on your side, so there was no competing Mega plan. There were no recorded decision errors, but the supplied evidence contains no Game 1 or between-game adjustment information, so whether an adjustment helped or backfired cannot be determined.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent, preserve Sneasler until Mega Alakazam is removed or unable to target it, and avoid presenting it after Icy Wind has compromised its speed. Build the game plan around denying Milotic repeated Recover turns rather than trading damage into it indefinitely; use the strongest available immediate pressure or double-targeting opportunities before it can stabilize. Treat Altaria's Cloud Nine as unreliable because Mega Alakazam can Trace it, and expect Taunt plus Icy Wind to disrupt its support role. The registered alternatives have no supplied sets or battle evidence, so there is not enough support to claim that the full roster contained a materially better four; replacing a vulnerable slot may be worth testing, but the change should be based on verified sets rather than assumed qualities. No between-game adjustment can be judged from the provided record.
reflections.notebook: Mega Alakazam revealed Psychic, Shadow Ball, Taunt, and Protect; it is a priority target, and Sneasler should not be exposed to it before it is removed or safely controlled. Mega Alakazam can Trace Altaria's Cloud Nine, so Cloud Nine should not be treated as an uncontestable advantage. Talonflame carries Focus Sash and Gale Wings and has Tailwind, Taunt, Brave Bird, and Flare Blitz; expect immediate speed-control or disruption pressure. Milotic carries Competitive, Sitrus Berry, Scald, Icy Wind, Haze, and Recover. It repeatedly uses Icy Wind to control speed and Recover to reset damage, so passive super-effective pressure from Archaludon is insufficient unless Recover turns are denied; Scald burn is a serious endgame threat. Scrafty carries Intimidate, Fake Out, Close Combat, Knock Off, Protect, and Lum Berry, providing early disruption and physical pressure. The opponent's core plan combines speed control, Taunt, defensive recovery, and strong special-attack punishment. Future preparation should prioritize reliable answers to Mega Alakazam and Milotic, preserve late-game attackers, and verify whether any unbrought roster member has a concrete advantage before changing the four.
